title: Anthropic's threat monitoring flags a Bonita Springs woman's messages about shooting up the Lee County Sheriff's Office; human reviewers tip police, who detain her without incident and seize no weapon
summary: Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged a chat user's threat to shoot up a Florida sheriff's office, and after human review the tip led deputies to detain her; no weapon was seized.
account: A user of Anthropic's AI chat service wrote at about 05:10 on 26 September 2026. She said that she was going to “shoot up” the Lee County Sheriff's Office in Florida. At 01:07 on 27 September she wrote that she had got a new gun. Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged the messages, and because of their severity a human review team reported them to law enforcement. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, reported that the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. The sheriff's office logged the tip on 29 September and identified the user as Carli Michelle Heller, 30, of Bonita Springs. Deputies detained her at home without incident at 00:51 on 30 September. A detective charged her under Florida Statute 836.10, written threats of violence. No weapon was seized, and she described the AI as a personal diary. The arrest report calls the platform “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Press reports name Claude, and court records note that the user told the detective that she used Perplexity. The arrest form set a $10,000 bond and a 20 October 2026 appearance date. Heller pleaded not guilty, and her arraignment was set for 2 November 2026 while prosecutors had not yet filed a formal charge. The First Amendment scholar Eugene Volokh doubts that the charge will hold.
purpose: Anthropic's consumer terms (effective 8 October 2025) reserve the right “at our sole discretion” to report Inputs to law enforcement. Its privacy policy (effective 10 September 2026) allows disclosure the company believes “reasonably necessary” to “prevent serious harm to any person or to property”. The arrest report says the platform's safety measures are “designed to monitor for key phrases and potentially threatening content”. Flagging a stated shooting threat, reviewing it by hand and referring it to police was that purpose. Of an August 2026 referral Anthropic said “This is our safeguards process working as intended”.
system: Anthropic Claude consumer-chat safety monitoring: automated flagging of threatening content, escalation to a human review team, referral to law enforcement
domain: Online safety and threat referral to law enforcement

ratings.reason: The Lee County Sheriff's Office, the threatened party, received a tip quoting a stated plan to shoot up its building and a claimed new gun. It identified the user and detained her at home without incident the day after it logged the tip. No weapon was seized, so no averted attack is shown.

Police examined a written threat of a mass shooting at a public building within days. It was at least the third Anthropic referral to police since August 2026. The benefit is limited because no weapon was found and the user described the chats as a personal diary. Experts doubt that the words were a true threat.

ai_role.statement: The arrest report says the platform “utilizes safety and security measures designed to monitor for key phrases and potentially threatening content”. It says the messages were “escalated to a human review team”. An automated layer therefore surfaced the two messages, and people judged their severity and made the referral. The sources do not say whether the flag came from a classifier or a keyword rule. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, says the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. Identifying the user, the home visit, the Miranda interview and the charging decision were the work of Lee County deputies and Intelligence Detective Thomas Alejo. The arrest report calls the platform “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Press reports name Claude, and court records note the user told the detective she used Perplexity.

produced_by: A vendor practice of screening consumer chats for threatening content and escalating severe cases to a human review team. That team can refer them to law enforcement, which Anthropic's consumer terms and privacy policy permit
A tip carrying enough account information for the sheriff's office to identify a named resident within days
A local agency that treated a stated threat against its own building as credible enough to send deputies the same night
must_hold: The referral must identify a real person and a real risk. The Lee County Sheriff's Office told reporters it does not count tips from Anthropic. No public figures exist on how often such referrals are made or prove unfounded

The disclosure must stay within the emergency exception of the Stored Communications Act. An EFF attorney told Straight Arrow News “there is always the risk of over-reporting”, and the Monitor logs reputational and psychological harm to the user

The response must remain proportionate. Here no weapon was found, and the user described a personal diary. Whether a chatbot prompt is a punishable threat under Florida Statute 836.10 is contested by the defense and by Eugene Volokh

The attribution to Claude rests on press reports and the arrest report's phrase “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Court records also note the user told the detective she used Perplexity, and her attorney declined to say which

echoes.setting: San Antonio, Texas: queries in an Anthropic chat about shooting at a nearby elementary school reached police through the FBI, and a 22-year-old man was arrested on a felony terroristic threat charge (Tom's Hardware, 5 October 2026).

San Francisco: a Claude user threatened Anthropic's CEO and said that he had bought an AR-15; Anthropic notified police, and the user was neither arrested nor charged and called it a misunderstanding.

Florida: OpenAI reported a ChatGPT user who wrote about killing his ex-girlfriend to the FBI; he pleaded guilty in August 2026 to written threats to kill under Florida Statute 836.10 and received eight years' probation (Tom's Hardware, citing the Palm Beach Post).

fields.summary: Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged a chat user's threat to shoot up a Florida sheriff's office, and after human review the tip led deputies to detain her; no weapon was seized.
fields.account: A user of Anthropic's AI chat service wrote at about 05:10 on 26 September 2026. She said that she was going to “shoot up” the Lee County Sheriff's Office in Florida. At 01:07 on 27 September she wrote that she had got a new gun. Anthropic's safety monitoring flagged the messages, and because of their severity a human review team reported them to law enforcement. Straight Arrow News, citing court records, reported that the review team escalated to the FBI, which notified the sheriff's office. The sheriff's office logged the tip on 29 September and identified the user as Carli Michelle Heller, 30, of Bonita Springs. Deputies detained her at home without incident at 00:51 on 30 September. A detective charged her under Florida Statute 836.10, written threats of violence. No weapon was seized, and she described the AI as a personal diary. The arrest report calls the platform “Anthropic Artificial Intelligence”. Press reports name Claude, and court records note that the user told the detective that she used Perplexity. The arrest form set a $10,000 bond and a 20 October 2026 appearance date. Heller pleaded not guilty, and her arraignment was set for 2 November 2026 while prosecutors had not yet filed a formal charge. The First Amendment scholar Eugene Volokh doubts that the charge will hold.

value.text: Monitoring triggered human escalation rather than an automatic arrest. The police investigator independently identified, interviewed, and charged the user.
